lifecycles._note: Light governance lifecycle for loggingaudit (audit trails / CloudTrail-equivalent). Covers all 6 uncovered writes: createtrail(POST /v1/trails), settrail(PUT /v1/trails/{trail_id}), starttrail(POST /v1/trails/{trail_id}/start), stoptrail(POST /v1/trails/{trail_id}/stop), deletetrail(DELETE /v1/trails/{trail_id}), downloadlogs(POST /v1/logs/download). No data/api_bodies.json entry for loggingaudit and docs are JS-rendered, so create/set bodies (target object-storage bucket + log selectors) are BEST-GUESS and UNPROVEN — promote after a real 2xx. createtrail typically requires a real object-storage bucket to receive logs, so a 400/403/422 is expected on a shared account; every mutating step is optional with a broad expect_status so it RECORDS coverage without failing. trail_id capture path $.trail.id is a guess; if absent the id-bound steps still normalize to the catalog '*' key. start/stop are POSTs without a body. downloadlogs is a coverage-only POST (it may stream a file on success; we only assert it is reachable). DELETE is destructive (gated).

steps.name: create-trail
steps._note: Body from api_docs.json request_example (createtrail, 2026-06-20). Field names confirmed: trail_name (not name), bucket_name (not object_storage_bucket_name), bucket_region (required, uses {region} placeholder to match trail region — bucket region immutable post-create per validated-facts). Shared test OBS bucket = do-not-delete-apitest (owner-provisioned, do NOT delete). All yn-flag arrays are required per doc schema. Response envelope: $.trail.id (confirmed by response_example). tags[] receives owner tags via engine. Capture $.trail.id -> trail_id unlocks the 5 id-bound sub-ops (show/set/start/stop/delete trail).

steps.name: set-trail
steps._note: Body from api_docs.json settrail request_example (2026-06-20). No bucket_name/bucket_region on update (immutable). Fields match the PUT schema: trail_description, trail_save_type, and all yn-flag arrays.

steps.name: delete-trail
steps._note: If create captured no id, {trail_id} stays literal and the DELETE normalizes to the catalog '*' key (records coverage) and 404s harmlessly.

steps.name: download-logs
steps._note: Coverage-only POST. Body UNPROVEN (downloadlogs likely takes a trail/time-window selector). On success it may return a download URL or stream; we only assert reachability. Isolated group so a 4xx never affects the trail group.

lifecycles._note: Light, READ-ONLY (no writes, no cleanup). Closes the static id-bound GET gap GET /v1/logs/{logging_id} (showlog) by the list->soft-capture->show idiom (the same pattern iam-readonly-shows uses). The trail node captures trail_id, NOT logging_id, so the trail lifecycle never satisfies this GET. listlogs (GET /v1/logs) REQUIRES start_at + end_at query params (ISO-8601 UTC, e.g. 2025-11-28T08:00:00Z, per service constraint listlogs-needs-time-window in knowledge/formal/services/management__loggingaudit.yaml); resource_id/resource_name/user_name/page/size/sort are optional. We send a WIDE static valid window (2025-01-01..2026-12-31, literal so it renders verbatim — the {today} builtin is %Y%m%d, NOT the ISO-8601 the param needs, so it is deliberately NOT used here) and soft-capture the first log entry's id ($.logs[0].id; LogListResponse.logs[] -> Log.id, response_example $.log.id confirms the id field name). A fresh account may have NO activity logs in the window (empty list) -> the {logging_id} segment stays a {placeholder} (normalizes to the catalog '*' key so the show is still CALLED and the endpoint statically reachable, 4xx-ing harmlessly). Both steps optional with tolerant [200,400,403,404]: a missing/invalid window 400s, denial 403s, empty list -> show 404s — every case still RECORDS coverage. The show returns LogShowResponse{log:Log}.

steps.name: list-logs
steps._note: listlogs with the REQUIRED start_at + end_at time window (ISO-8601 UTC) sent via params (service constraint listlogs-needs-time-window). A wide static window maximises the chance the account has at least one activity log to soft-capture ($.logs[0].id, LogListResponse.logs[].id). Tolerant [200,400,403,404]: empty/denied/missing-window all still let the show below be CALLED.

steps.name: show-log
steps._note: id-bound read (showlog). Closes GAP-get-id for GET /v1/logs/{logging_id}. Keys off the list-captured logging_id (a real id when the window has any logs -> 2xx); if the window is empty the segment stays a placeholder (normalizes to catalog '*') and 4xx's. Tolerant [200,400,403,404]; the GET is CALLED so the endpoint is statically reachable.
